title: Phosphoproteomic and Kinomic Signature of Clinically Aggressive Grade I (1.5) Meningiomas Reveals RB1 Signaling as a Novel Mediator and Biomarker

publications.title: Phosphoproteomic and Kinomic Signature of Clinically Aggressive Grade I (1.5) Meningiomas Reveals RB1 Signaling as a Novel Mediator and Biomarker.

institution: University of Washington School of Medicine (Dept. of Neurosurgery / Dept. of Pathology), Seattle
platform: iTRAQ 4-plex isobaric labeling LC-MS/MS (phosphoproteomics, Table S6); PamStation/peptide-chip kinome array (Table S7)

brain_invasion.counts: Invasion column present in Table S3/S4 per-sample annotation ('yes'/'no'/'NA'); exact aggregate counts not tabulated in this review, present at the individual-sample level in the downloaded file

anatomic_location_breakdown: Per-sample free-text location field in Table S3/S4 (e.g. left orbital roof/basal frontal, right parietal parafalcine, extra-axial foramen magnum, falx and parasagittal, convexity, CPA); not aggregated into the controlled vocabulary's anatomic categories here
sex_distribution: Reported per-sample in Table S3/S4 'Demography' free-text field (e.g. '75 F'); not aggregated in this review
age_distribution: Reported per-sample in Table S3/S4 'Demography' free-text field; not aggregated in this review
processed_data_format: Two per-sample clinical/pathology annotation tables (Table S3, Table S4, xlsx), one MS/MS phosphopeptide identification/quantification table with iTRAQ4plex + phospho modifications (Table S6, xlsx, 649 peptide-spectrum rows), and one kinome peptide-array signal-intensity table (Table S7, xlsx, 101 peptides x grade-group signal intensity/fold-change/p-value)
needs_manual_review_reason: Directly downloaded and inspected 4 of the 5 figshare items named in the extraction task (Table S3, S4, S6, S7); Table S8 (10.1158/1078-0432.22471818.v1) was checked and EXCLUDED from this record because it is an Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) enrichment-analysis export derived from the other tables' results, not itself a primary molecular dataset. MODALITY CHOICE: this study combines (a) MS-based iTRAQ phosphoproteomics (Table S6) and (b) a kinome peptide-chip array (Table S7, PamStation-style, signal intensity per peptide substrate per grade group -- NOT per-individual-sample, only group-level averages for Grade1/Grade1.5/Grade1.5-1 are present in the deposited file). Neither this project's controlled_vocabulary.md nor any existing modality cleanly covers a kinome peptide-substrate array; 'proteomics_bulk_ms' was used as the closest available fit for the whole record per instructions, but this likely undercounts the distinctiveness of the kinome-array component -- recommend the project consider a dedicated 'kinome_array' (or similar) controlled-vocabulary value if more kinome-profiling datasets are added. SAMPLE-COUNT AMBIGUITY: Table S3 (n=85 valid rows after removing 4 blank trailer rows) mixes Grade I (31), Grade 1.5 (19), Grade II (26+1 annotated variant), and Grade III (4) samples in one per-sample TMA-style annotation table with a near-empty 'Discovery Set?' flag column (only 1 of 85 rows marked 'Yes'), so the exact discovery-cohort vs. independent-TMA-validation-cohort (140 samples per the paper's abstract) split could NOT be cleanly resolved from the deposited spreadsheet alone; Table S4 is a separate, overlapping-but-distinct 59-row table (Grade 1.5=22, I=19, II=18) that additionally carries per-sample NF2/TRAF7/AKT1/KLF4/SMO genotyping. Given this ambiguity, patient_count/sample_count are reported as Table S3's row count (85) as the single largest coherently-countable per-sample table, with the caveat that Table S4's 59-row cohort is a separate/overlapping set not additively combined into this figure (to avoid double-counting patients who may appear in both tables under different IDs). grade_breakdown uses Table S3's counts. has_outcome_data=true is based on directly-observed 'Ability to Recur/Progress' and 'Time of Recurrence/Progression (months)' columns present in both S3 and S4 (not inferred from the abstract), but recurrence_annotated was left false since these columns record eventual outcome per sample rather than an explicit primary-vs-recurrent sample-type split. brain_invasion.status_reported=true reflects a genuine 'Invasion' column in the data, though determination method (e.g. histologic criteria used) is not stated in the spreadsheet, so brain_invasion_annotated tag is false per the tag's own definition (requires a stated determination method). tags.large_cohort is set false regardless of this cohort's actual size, per instruction that large_cohort requires centralized recomputation across the whole inventory after this extraction batch, not a per-record judgment. RE-VERIFICATION AUDIT 2026-07-12: re-downloaded all four figshare items and re-tabulated directly. Table S7's peptide count in processed_data_format was corrected from 103 to 101 (the deposited sheet has peptides numbered 1 through 101; the prior 103 counted the two header rows as data). Table S3 (85 clinical rows: Grade I=31, Grade 1.5=19, Grade II=26 plus 1 atypical-variant, Grade III=4), Table S4 (59 rows with NF2/TRAF7/AKT1/KLF4/SMO), and Table S6 (649 peptide-spectrum rows) all re-confirmed exactly. Publication (PMID 31615938) re-verified: 15 authors, corresponding author Manuel Ferreira (email manuelf3@uw.edu), all match.
